what: Chime is an American banking app. It has no branches and holds no banking licence of its own: partner banks hold the deposits, and Chime earns most of its money from the fees merchants pay when customers use its debit cards.
customers: Americans earning roughly $35,000 to $75,000 a year, many of whom were charged overdraft fees by traditional banks.
money: interchange fees on debit and credit card spending
instant transfer fees, lending and other services
moat: Customers who route their salary into the account. Direct deposit makes an account the one people actually use, and moving it is enough effort that most never do.
risks: Interchange fees are set by card networks and have been a target for regulators before
A 2.1% margin after costs: the model needs enormous scale to earn much per customer
SoFi and Cash App offer similar accounts and compete for the same customers
opportunities: $418M of free cash flow and $1.1B of cash against $135M of debt
Revenue grew from $1.3B to $2.2B in two years
Analysts see about 37% upside, with 21 covering the stock
watch: Active members with direct deposit and revenue per active member.
